WARN "payment.declined" records, each carrying the saga trace_id
decline rate at 100% — payment.requests with result=declined only
saga trace shows payment.declined -> compensation -> order CANCELLED (one correlated trace across the NATS hops)

label.remediation: Cleared PAYMENT_FAILURE_RATE (back to the authorize-all default) and recreated the Payment container; subsequent checkouts authorized and confirmed normally. The orders cancelled during the window require manual reconciliation. Durable fix: alert on a sustained decline-rate spike and add a saga-level retry/backoff for transient declines before compensating.
label.root_cause: The Payment simulator was configured to decline 100% of authorizations (PAYMENT_FAILURE_RATE=1.0), so every order's payment.authorize was answered with payment.declined (do_not_honor). The Orders saga treated each decline as terminal, ran compensation (released the inventory reservation), and moved the order to CANCELLED — no order in the window could reach CONFIRMED.

title: Payment latency spike — slow authorizations inflate the saga

symptoms.description: notification.messages stops incrementing for the window (flat), then a catch-up burst on recovery
orders.confirmed events still emitted with NO matching notification.sent (producer up, consumer down)
the notification log stream goes silent during the window (no consume records)
sample: shutdown signal received; stopping subscriber and health server

symptoms.description: saga traces still reach CONFIRMED, but no `consume orders.confirmed` span joins them

label.remediation: Started the Notification worker again; its durable consumer redelivered the pending terminal events and caught up (a notification.sent burst). Durable fix: alert on consumer-count = 0 / rising consumer-pending for the ORDERS stream so a stalled fan-out is detected before notices are missed for hours.
label.root_cause: The Notification worker (a durable JetStream consumer on orders.confirmed / orders.cancelled) was stopped. The checkout saga is independent of it, so orders still reached CONFIRMED — but the terminal events accumulated unconsumed on the ORDERS stream and no notification.sent was emitted. A silent failure: no HTTP error, no crash, just a broken fan-out tail.

title: Notification worker down — orders confirm but no notice is sent

symptoms.description: rpc.server.duration p99 for catalogue climbs well above its sub-10ms baseline
ListProducts spans and their pgx query child spans run long against the throttled DB
cascade — BFF /api/products request duration p99 rises in step
elevated request-handling latency in catalogue logs, each carrying trace_id

label.remediation: Removed the CPU cap (dropped the override and recreated Postgres uncapped); query latency returned to baseline. Durable fix: guarantee DB CPU/IO, add slow-query logging and an index review, and bound the catalogue connection pool + add a read cache so a starved DB sheds load instead of cascading to every browse request.
label.root_cause: Postgres was CPU-capped to 0.1 of a core while product-browse load ran. The Catalogue service stayed up but its ListProducts SELECTs queued on the starved database, so product-listing latency climbed sharply (a throttle, not a crash — pods remained Running). The latency cascaded to the BFF and the storefront read path.
